edition_title: Immersive art became an anchor tenant
subject: Immersive art is pulling millions and anchoring real estate

hero.statement: Immersive art became an anchor tenant
hero.sub: The digital art room stopped being a pop up. It is now a permanent institution that developers build cities around.

sections.statement: teamLab drew millions to a single museum
sections.body: teamLab Borderless, reopened in Tokyo's Azabudai Hills with more than 75 works, welcomed about 1.69 million visitors in 2025. Across its two Tokyo museums teamLab pulled over 4.2 million people in a year, a footfall most retail anchors would envy.
sections.why: Footfall like that turns an art room into a leasing magnet. Immersive is becoming the anchor, not the amenity.

sections.statement: Europe is building its largest immersive room
sections.body: In Hamburg, the UBS Digital Art Museum opens in spring 2026 as Europe's largest home for digital art: 6,500 square metres, 12 metre ceilings, with a permanent teamLab Borderless as its star. A bank put its name on an immersive museum. That is the tell.
sections.why: When institutions and banks anchor around immersive art, the category has left the experiment phase for good.

sections.statement: People pay to walk inside the work
sections.body: The draw is not a wall you look at. It is a space that reacts to your footsteps, water you wade through, light that answers your body. The visitor is inside the piece, not in front of it.
sections.why: Participation is the product. The experiences that let people act, not just watch, are the ones that sell tickets.

invitation.headline: Give the brand a room worth entering
invitation.body: The immersive room that draws crowds is one people can step inside and change. We design responsive, walk in environments for brands and agencies, white label, under your name.
